name: Mahasthangarh
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 18 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel north from Bogura city toward Shibganj and Mahasthan. CNG, auto-rickshaw, local bus and private vehicles are commonly used. From the Mahasthan area, the archaeological site is easily accessible by local transport.
description: Mahasthangarh is the most important archaeological and historical attraction in Bogura district. It is identified with the ancient city of Pundranagara or Pundravardhana and represents one of the earliest urban settlements in Bangladesh. Archaeological evidence indicates that the settlement existed from the third century BCE and continued through several historical periods. The fortified area contains remains associated with Maurya, Gupta, Pala, Sena and later periods. The site includes ancient ramparts, temples, residential structures, religious monuments, wells and other archaeological remains. Its position beside the Karatoya River also contributed to its historical importance as a centre of administration, trade and culture. Visitors can explore the ancient fortified city and several nearby archaeological monuments in the same trip. Mahasthangarh is also closely connected with the Mahasthan Archaeological Museum, Gokul Medh, Govinda Bhita, Khodar Pathar Bhita and Jiyat Kunda. Because of its exceptional archaeological value, it is the central heritage destination of Bogura and one of the major archaeological attractions of Bangladesh.

name: Mahasthan Archaeological Museum
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 18 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Take a bus, CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle from Bogura city toward Mahasthangarh. The museum is located near the main archaeological site.
description: The Mahasthan Archaeological Museum preserves archaeological objects discovered from Mahasthangarh and surrounding sites. Its collection represents different historical periods and provides visitors with a clearer understanding of the ancient civilization that developed around Pundranagara. The museum contains sculptures, terracotta objects, pottery, coins, inscriptions, metal objects, ornaments and other archaeological materials. A visit to the museum is especially useful before or after exploring Mahasthangarh because many of the objects found through archaeological excavation are preserved and displayed here. The museum therefore acts as an important interpretation centre for the archaeological heritage of Bogura. Visitors interested in ancient Bengal, Buddhism, Hindu religious traditions, architecture, sculpture and everyday life can find valuable material here. It is one of the most important cultural attractions to include in a Bogura tourism database.

name: Gokul Medh
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 10 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel north from Bogura city toward Gokul village. CNG, auto-rickshaw and private vehicles can be used. It is also approximately 1.5–2 km south of Mahasthangarh.
description: Gokul Medh is an important archaeological mound in Gokul village of Bogura Sadar. It is popularly known as Behula-Lakhindar Basar Ghar because of its connection with the famous Bengali folklore of Behula and Lakhindar. Archaeological excavation revealed the remains of multi-level brick structures and ancient architectural features. The site has been interpreted by scholars through archaeological evidence rather than solely through the popular folklore surrounding it. The monument is close to Mahasthangarh and is therefore an important part of the archaeological tourism circuit of Bogura. Visitors can combine Gokul Medh with Mahasthangarh and other nearby archaeological sites. The mound is surrounded by the rural landscape of Bogura and offers an opportunity to experience both archaeology and local cultural traditions. The government tourism portal identifies Gokul Medh as an archaeological site in Gokul village, while the Bogura district administration describes excavated brick structures and multiple construction phases at the site.

name: Vasu Vihara
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 25 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel toward Mahasthangarh and then continue toward Bihar village in Shibganj. CNG, auto-rickshaw and private vehicles are suitable.
description: Vasu Vihara is one of the most important Buddhist archaeological sites in Bogura. It is located in Bihar village of Shibganj and is locally known as Narapatir Dhap. Archaeological excavation revealed the remains of Buddhist monastic structures, including rectangular monasteries and a temple. Excavations produced terracotta plaques, bronze Buddhist images, seals, decorated bricks, beads, lamps and other archaeological objects. The remains demonstrate the importance of Buddhism in the ancient and early medieval history of the Bogura region. Vasu Vihara is generally visited as part of the Mahasthangarh archaeological circuit. Its peaceful rural setting and ancient brick structures make it especially attractive to visitors interested in archaeology and Buddhist heritage. The site provides important evidence about the religious and educational institutions that existed in northern Bengal in earlier centuries.

name: Govinda Bhita
location: Near Mahasthangarh, beside the Karatoya River
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 18 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel to Mahasthangarh by bus, CNG or private vehicle and then use local transport or walk to Govinda Bhita.
description: Govinda Bhita is an archaeological mound located near the fortified area of Mahasthangarh beside the Karatoya River. Archaeological excavation revealed the remains of a temple structure and evidence of rebuilding during different periods. Excavation has also produced ancient coins, terracotta objects and other archaeological materials. The site's location near the river and the main fortified city makes it an important component of the Mahasthangarh heritage circuit. Visitors interested in ancient architecture can observe the remains and understand how religious structures formed part of the ancient urban landscape. Govinda Bhita is generally included with Mahasthangarh, the archaeological museum, Gokul Medh and other nearby sites during a heritage tour of Bogura.

name: Khodar Pathar Bhita
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 18 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel to Mahasthangarh and then use local transport to reach the archaeological mound.
description: Khodar Pathar Bhita is an archaeological mound within the wider Mahasthangarh area. Excavation at the site revealed the remains of an ancient temple or religious structure and several archaeological objects. A large granite stone doorway discovered at the mound is associated with the popular local name of the site. Archaeologists also discovered Buddhist images and other remains during excavation. The site provides additional evidence of the religious and architectural diversity of ancient Mahasthangarh. Although smaller than the main fortified city, it is an important stop for visitors who want to explore the archaeological landscape beyond the central ruins.

name: Jiyat Kunda
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 18 km north of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel to Mahasthangarh and continue to the Jiyat Kunda area using local transport.
description: Jiyat Kunda is an ancient water structure associated with the historical and folkloric traditions of Mahasthangarh. Local tradition connects the site with King Parashuram and Shah Sultan Balkhi. According to popular legend, the water of the well possessed extraordinary powers. Although these supernatural claims belong to folklore rather than established archaeological fact, the site remains culturally important because of its connection with the legends surrounding Mahasthangarh. Jiyat Kunda is best visited together with the main Mahasthangarh archaeological attractions.

name: Kherua Mosque
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 30 km southwest of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel from Bogura city toward Sherpur on the Dhaka-Bogura highway. From Sherpur town, continue approximately 1 km southwest toward Khandakar Tola by CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle.
description: Kherua Mosque is one of the most significant historical mosques in Bogura district. It is located in Khandakar Tola of Sherpur and dates to the late sixteenth century. The mosque is notable for its thick brick walls, three domes, arched entrances and decorated mihrabs. Its architectural form reflects the transition and interaction between regional Sultanate traditions and Mughal-period architectural styles. The mosque has survived for centuries and remains an important example of early Islamic architecture in northern Bangladesh. Its rural surroundings provide a contrast to the dense urban environment of Bogura. Visitors can combine a visit to Kherua Mosque with other historical attractions around Sherpur. The mosque is particularly important for visitors interested in architecture, Islamic history and heritage conservation.

name: Kali Tala Ghat
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 22 km east of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel east from Bogura city toward Sariakandi. CNG, auto-rickshaw, local transport and private vehicles can be used. Continue toward the Kali Tala riverbank.
description: Kali Tala Ghat is a popular riverside attraction in Sariakandi. The site is located beside the Jamuna River and provides visitors with open natural scenery, river views, boats and seasonal chars. The riverbank is especially attractive during the cooler months when the weather is suitable for outdoor travel. Visitors can take boat trips and observe the changing landscape of the Jamuna. The area also provides an opportunity to experience the river-based lifestyle of people living along one of Bangladesh's major rivers. Kali Tala Ghat is different from the archaeological attractions of northern Bogura because its main attraction is natural landscape and river culture.

name: Prem Jamuna Ghat
boguraSadarDistance: Approximately 22 km east of Bogura city
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel from Bogura city toward Sariakandi and continue to the Jamuna riverbank. CNG, auto-rickshaw and private vehicles are suitable.
description: Prem Jamuna Ghat is a scenic riverside destination in Sariakandi where visitors can experience the broad landscape of the Jamuna River. The location is particularly attractive for people interested in river scenery, boating and photography. Seasonal chars appear in the river and create changing landscapes throughout the year. The nearby embankment was developed primarily for riverbank protection but has also become a recreational destination for local visitors. Prem Jamuna Ghat can be visited together with Kali Tala Ghat as both attractions are located in the Sariakandi river area.

name: Karatoya River
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: The river can be accessed from several points around Bogura city and the Mahasthangarh archaeological area.
description: The Karatoya River is closely connected with the historical development of Bogura. Mahasthangarh, the ancient city of Pundranagara, developed beside the river, making the waterway an important part of the area's historical landscape. Today the river and its surrounding areas remain culturally and geographically significant. The river can be included in a broader Bogura heritage itinerary together with Mahasthangarh and other archaeological sites. The attraction is primarily natural and cultural rather than a conventional enclosed tourist site.

name: Bogura DC Park
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel through the central Bogura city area toward Jail Bridge. The park is accessible by rickshaw, auto-rickshaw, CNG and private vehicle.
description: Bogura DC Park is an urban recreational destination in Bogura city. It provides residents and visitors with an open environment for leisure, walking and family outings. Unlike the archaeological sites of Shibganj, the park represents the modern recreational side of Bogura. Its location close to the city centre makes it easy to include in a city tour. The park is suitable for visitors who want a short recreational break after visiting historical and cultural attractions.

name: Wonderland Park Bogura
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel through the city toward Stadium Road. Rickshaw, CNG, auto-rickshaw and private vehicles are available.
description: Wonderland Park is a recreational and amusement destination in Bogura city. It provides entertainment facilities for families and children and is different from the district's archaeological and historical destinations. Because it is located inside the city, it can easily be included in a one-day Bogura city itinerary. The park is particularly suitable for families looking for recreational activities after visiting museums, historical sites and other attractions.

name: Thompson Hall
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel along Sherpur Road using rickshaw, CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle.
description: Thompson Hall is a historic landmark in Bogura city and forms part of the district's urban heritage. The building represents an older period of civic and institutional development in Bogura. It is especially relevant for visitors interested in the architectural and cultural history of the city rather than only ancient archaeology. Its central location makes it convenient to visit with other Bogura city landmarks.

name: Sathmatha Bir Sreshtho Square
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Sathmatha is located in the central part of Bogura city and can easily be reached by rickshaw, CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle.
description: Sathmatha is one of the most recognizable central landmarks of Bogura city. The Bir Sreshtho Square area functions as an important urban gathering and orientation point. It is useful for visitors exploring Bogura city because many important commercial, cultural and civic locations are situated around the central area. The square can be included in a city sightseeing route together with historic buildings, libraries, parks and other urban landmarks.

name: Woodburn Public Library
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Reach the central Bogura city area by rickshaw, CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle.
description: Woodburn Public Library is one of the notable cultural institutions associated with the history of Bogura city. The Bogura Sadar government tourism information identifies the library as an old institution established in the nineteenth century. Its importance lies in the literary and intellectual history of the city. For a heritage-focused tourism website, the library can be presented alongside other historical civic landmarks rather than as a conventional recreational tourist spot. It provides an opportunity to explore the educational and literary development of Bogura.

name: Chand Saudagar Homestead
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel toward Chadmuhar-Haripur area using local CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle. Local directions may be required because it is a rural heritage location.
description: The Chand Saudagar Homestead is identified by the Bogura Sadar government tourism information as a local historical and folkloric attraction. Chand Saudagar is a famous figure in Bengali Manasamangal literature, and sites associated with the character are preserved in local traditions. The attraction is more strongly connected with folklore and cultural memory than with confirmed archaeological identification. It can therefore be presented on a heritage website as a folkloric site while clearly distinguishing legend from archaeological evidence. The location provides an opportunity to explore the relationship between Bengali literature, oral tradition and the cultural landscape of Bogura.

name: Padma Devi House
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel toward Namuja Union and then continue to Chingaspur village by local transport or private vehicle.
description: Padma Devi House in Chingaspur is included among the historical and culturally significant places listed by the Bogura Sadar government portal. The site is associated with local traditional stories and cultural memory. Unlike the major archaeological monuments of Mahasthangarh, its importance is primarily folkloric and local. A district tourism database should preserve this distinction while still including the site because it forms part of the documented cultural heritage of Bogura Sadar.

name: Kalu Gazi's Kot
location: Raymajhira area, Lahiri Para Union, Bogura Sadar
howToGoFromBoguraSadar: Travel toward Lahiri Para Union and continue to the Raymajhira area by CNG, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle.
description: Kalu Gazi's Kot in the Raymajhira area is listed by the Bogura Sadar government portal as a local historical attraction. The site forms part of the lesser-known heritage landscape of Bogura Sadar. Such locations are valuable for a district tourism database because they document local history beyond the major nationally recognized archaeological monuments. The site can be included in rural heritage tours, although visitors should verify local access conditions before travelling.
